description: A profile that watches a named competitor set is given the competitor register. Firms have newsrooms worth proposing; a category entry names no single organisation and has none, and inventing one would send a probe at an address that cannot exist.

input.topic: Competitor public positioning read against Canvas's five competency pillars
input.watchlist_note: Competitor site copy, case studies, LinkedIn posts and partner-badge pages, read one pillar at a time.

competitors.name: the Big Four SA data practices

expected_output.shape: single JSON object with keys profile_id, candidates
expected_output.no_candidate_for: the Big Four SA data practices

rubric.criterion: No source is proposed for a category
rubric.condition: No candidate's `publisher` field equals an input competitor whose `kind` is "category" — exactly 0 candidates may name "the Big Four SA data practices", which is a category and has no newsroom.

rubric.criterion: Reconstructed newsroom addresses are honest about it
rubric.condition: Every candidate whose `url` is a reconstructed address rather than a recalled page has `confidence` equal to the exact string "low", never "medium" or "high".
The candidates span at least 3 distinct publishers, so a competitor-set profile does not end up reading one vendor's own publishing.

notes: Anchored to prompt.md hard rule 10 and its Method paragraph on competitor-set profiles. The competitor list comes from functions/_shared/competitor-register.yaml, which carries no urls on purpose.
